key_insight: An LLM-guided evolutionary search discovered quantum circuits that outperform the state of the art on most benchmark tasks, including a new reversible architecture that makes modular inversion more efficient.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical path for co-designing quantum algorithms and circuits by automating circuit discovery under hardware-relevant constraints like Toffoli count and qubit count.
method: An independent evaluator verifies and scores each circuit.
The search is applied across numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory.
evidence_signal: Across eight tasks, seven showed significant reductions in both Toffoli and qubit counts versus the prior state of the art, and the eighth produced a new modular inversion architecture with a better Toffoli-qubit trade-off.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable evaluator design and benchmarking, so gains may be sensitive to the chosen task formulation, constraints, and verification cost.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
